verdicts.note: Attacked toward 0. S1 is mostly status quo ('maintaining essential services', 'support and maintain investments in critical infrastructure') and adds 'modernizing systems to improve efficiency', which leans toward restraint. But S3 is a clear call for new money: 'Our community needs funds to address issues for youth and young families', naming completion of the pool project and child care. One clear statement toward pole_b, softened by S1, supports +1 medium. Nothing in the dossier points toward audits or cuts.

The basis quotes Warren as saying he can 'bring a stronger voice'. That phrase appears nowhere in his dossier, the contest dossier or the pamphlet text (S1), so the quoted evidence is unsupported. What remains is challenger status alone. He does not run on renewal: his pamphlet statement (S1) runs on nine years as a Walla Walla Community College trustee and current board chair, and on 'leadership in policy development, labor relations, and budget management'. He makes no anti-incumbent or new-voices case and never criticizes Miller in the dossier. Pole_b is 'outsider energy, generational change'. Being the non-incumbent keeps the direction at +1 relative to Miller, but confidence drops to low. Drop the 'stronger voice' quote from the basis. Warren's summary and highlights otherwise check out against S1, S3 and S5.

The direction is right. The only tax-position evidence is a single Q&A answer (S3): 'A problem for all citizens is over taxation ... Raising the income limit for property tax exemptions is a step in the right direction.' In the same answer he frames the county's role as 'spend money as efficiently as possible', not as cutting county taxes or opposing levies. The second citation, S1 (pamphlet, checked against the text), is about careful handling of tax dollars and positive cash flow. That is spending evidence, not a tax position. The dossier records no vote, pledge or plank on county levies or levy-cap lifts. Compare Walla Walla's Fulmer, who reached -2 only with a recorded no on cap relief plus three statements. Under the addendum's principle, ±2 needs a second independent tax source, so -1 medium. The basis also overstates S3: he calls over-taxation 'a problem for all citizens', not 'the main problem facing residents'. Display: the same overstatement appears in the first highlight ('the main problem for residents') and in the race_blurb ('names over-taxation as residents' main problem'). Suggested highlight: 'Says over-taxation is "a problem for all citizens" and backs raising the income limit for property tax exemptions [S3]'. Suggested blurb: '...a retired farmer who calls over-taxation a problem for all citizens...'.

S1 (verified against the pamphlet): 'My priority is always to maintain a positive cash flow', 'extremely careful in the handling of other people's money', 'spend carefully'. S3: 'spend money as efficiently as possible'. That is restraint without a concrete audit or cut proposal, so -1 rather than -2. Two sources support medium. The April 2025 vote to surplus and auction the old planning office (S10) is consistent with this but too thin to raise the score.

S1 (verified against the pamphlet): 'My track record of successfully managing business along with four years as county commissioner gives me the knowledge and ability to lead'. He is a one-term incumbent who beat the sitting commissioner in 2022 (S13). He runs on his record, but one term keeps it at -1. High holds on S1 alone, which is a direct, first-person campaign statement. Display: the highlight 'Says the new-commissioner learning curve "is now behind me" [S3]' is not in the pamphlet text, and the candidate dossier never records it in its body with a citation. It appears only in the scoring notes and in the contest dossier's paraphrase. Drop it, or replace it with the sourced 'Says four years as commissioner give him "the knowledge and ability to lead" [S1]'. The other Miller highlights and summary check out (S1, S3, S11, S13).
